## 開篇固定收益論點

7月24日美國公債收盤小幅牛市趨陡，扭轉此前連續3個交易日由前端領跌的走勢，但未逆轉本週對政策路徑的重新定價。2年期殖利率下降4個基點至4.33%，10年期下降2個基點至4.69%，30年期回落1個基點至5.16%。布蘭特原油突破100美元後回落至96.78美元，消除部分迫切的通膨壓力，政策敏感券種因而反彈最多。然而，各天期殖利率全週仍收高10至15個基點，10年期實質殖利率維持在2.43%，長債殖利率也仍處於近20年前的水準。

週五漲勢的結構決定了核心判讀。10年期名目殖利率下跌，完全來自損益兩平通膨率下降2個基點至2.26%；實質殖利率並未變動。油價單日下跌3.88%，減弱邊際通膨衝擊，但布蘭特原油1週仍上漲9.85%，1個月漲幅更達25.56%。市場定價Fed 7月升息的機率仍約35%，高於較溫和的6月CPI公布後約10%的水準。因此，前一交易日實質殖利率的升勢只是暫停，並未反轉；存續期間要出現持久漲勢，門檻依然很高。

通膨風險也從能源擴散至其他領域。華府重建部分關稅制度後，對來自約60個經濟體的進口商品課徵10%至12.5%關稅，措施已正式生效。美國服務業活動強韌、新屋銷售增加，削弱了經濟成長放緩足以支持快速寬鬆的論據；新增關稅又開啟未來商品價格上漲的傳導管道。截至收盤，關稅與油價都尚未證實基礎通膨再度加速。不過，兩項風險同時存在，加上Fed減少前瞻指引，使7月28日至29日的決策格外難以形成穩定預期，也讓美國公債預期波動率維持高檔。

信用市場走勢不支持系統性緊縮的解讀，但整體指標平靜，掩蓋了承接能力更重要的變化。投資級與高收益債券基金週五幾乎持平，但Meta資料中心專案的123億美元債券融資，最終訂單僅為發行額的1.6倍。長天期科技債供給正成為指數層級的存續期間問題：美國高評級債券的存續期間乘以利差風險中，6大科技借款人目前占8.6%，高於6大銀行的7.3%。資金仍可取得，但市場真正關注的已不只是信用品質，而是新券讓利、租約支持與集中度。

全球長債供給也進一步壓抑美國公債漲勢。英國10年期殖利率週五雖然回落，仍維持在5%以上；日本40年期殖利率上升10個基點至4.01%；全球投資級主權債基準平均殖利率升至3.68%，創2008年以來最高。ECB在油價上漲前進行的調查顯示，通膨預期與薪資成長放緩，但官員仍保留9月緊縮的可能性。因此，週五收盤只是一波受控的紓壓走勢，全球通膨、財政與資本供給環境仍要求異常高的實質殖利率。

## 美國公債利率、Fed定價、實質殖利率與曲線結構

美國公債依到期年限有序收復週四部分跌幅。2年期殖利率下降4個基點至4.33%，5年期下降3個基點至4.43%，10年期回落2個基點至4.69%，30年期下滑1個基點至5.16%。2s10s曲線陡化2個基點至36個基點，2s30s陡化3個基點至83個基點。前端表現優於長端，與前一交易日的熊市趨平恰好相反：原油回落壓低近期政策溢價，長端要求的補償卻更具黏性。

相較此前累積的賣壓，單日紓壓幅度有限。1週內，2年期與5年期殖利率均上升15個基點，10年期上升14個基點，30年期上升10個基點；1個月內，各天期則分別上升17、16、19與22個基點。週線仍反映市場大幅轉向較緊的政策路徑；月線則顯示長端升幅更大，因為財政融資、全球主權債供給與企業資本支出都在爭奪存續期間承接能力。

抗通膨美國公債顯示，週五漲勢是能源溢價回吐，而非實質利率門檻下降。10年期實質殖利率維持在2.43%，較1週前高12個基點，較1個月前高14個基點。10年期損益兩平通膨率下降2個基點至2.26%，全週僅上升2個基點。中期通膨指標受控、實質殖利率卻處於極高水準，顯示投資人並未放棄對長期物價控制的信心；但要實現這項結果，政策與成長前景仍有高度不確定性，投資人因而要求大幅補償。

油價路徑解釋了週五與全週表現的差異。布蘭特原油收在96.78美元，WTI收在89.31美元，單日分別下跌3.88%與3.12%；中東航線的實體流量持續，市場重啟斡旋的討論也略微緩解壓力。此前攻擊已使衝突從荷姆茲海峽擴及紅海航運，並推動布蘭特原油突破100美元。單日跌勢降低了通膨尾端風險的急迫性，但布蘭特原油與WTI全週分別上漲9.85%與8.27%，燃料、運費與庫存成本仍明顯高於前一個週五。

因此，即使殖利率下降，Fed定價仍呈不對稱。市場估計7月會議升息25個基點的機率約35%，反映油價高檔、新增關稅，以及主席Kevin Warsh減少使用前瞻指引所帶來的不確定性。35%的機率並不代表市場共識預期升息，而是結果分布較6月CPI公布後顯著擴大；當時市場定價機率已降至約10%。這股不確定性也將MOVE指數推升至5月以來最高。

美國國內經濟活動限制了週五漲勢。服務需求抵銷製造業降溫，使美國商業活動以8個月來最快速度擴張，新屋銷售也增加。這些訊號尚不足以證明經濟過熱，卻讓市場更難假設外部供給衝擊正發生在需求崩跌的環境。經濟活動強韌，讓Fed有更大空間優先處理未來通膨風險，也解釋了為何油價下跌雖推動2年期公債上漲，殖利率卻未回到本週情勢升級前的水準。

關稅則開啟一條速度較慢、不確定性也更高的傳導管道。10%至12.5%的關稅取代到期的10%全球進口稅，涵蓋約60個經濟體的商品。措施週五已生效，但對消費者物價、企業利潤率與貿易量的影響仍待浮現。對利率而言，眼前影響並非已實現的通膨數據，而是政策路徑的不確定範圍擴大；能源與進口成本可能相互強化，即使單獨來看，任一衝擊都可能只是暫時性。

長端仍是主要估值限制。30年期殖利率為5.16%，即使油價單日大跌也只下降1個基點；20年期以上美國公債指數1週仍下跌1.48%，1個月下跌4.39%。這種黏性符合當前市場環境：全球政府與科技發行人都要求同一批保險公司、退休基金與長存續期間基金承接更多供給。因此，週五殖利率曲線陡化代表前端紓壓，而非長債需求恢復寬鬆。

美國公債收盤走勢化解了單日殖利率下降與週線環境更具限制性之間的表面矛盾。損益兩平通膨率收斂促成部分反彈，但10年期實質殖利率不變、Fed不確定性居高不下，30年期殖利率也頑強維持高檔，使本次走勢無法演變為市場對政策或期限溢價的廣泛重估。若要持久反轉，能源與關稅兩條通膨管道必須持續降溫，或經濟活動明顯惡化，足以帶動實質殖利率下行。

## 信用、融資與初級市場承接

整體信用市場週五收盤未見風險溢價失序擴張。LQD下跌0.03%，HYG持平，JNK下跌0.01%。1個月內，LQD下跌2.46%，跌幅大於HYG的0.80%與JNK的0.89%，主要反映投資級債承受較重的存續期間壓力。整體市場信用利差仍接近多年來最窄水準。更具意義的訊號，來自市場承銷長天期AI基礎設施債務所要求的條件。

BlackRock規劃為Meta位於El Paso的資料中心園區融資，123億美元債券僅取得200億美元最終訂單，為發行額的1.6倍。債券透過Sopaipilla Investor發行，2048年到期，初步價格指引約為10年期美國公債殖利率加287.5個基點。相較2049年到期、條件相近的Beignet債券，新券讓利約寬40個基點；後者利差在7月已擴大逾50個基點。交易預計7月27日定價，週五收盤前尚未完成。

交易結構提供實質債權人保障，卻未消除集中度問題。募集資金將用於興建預計可提供最高1吉瓦運算容量的園區。BlackRock旗下子公司持有專案80%，Meta持有20%。特殊目的公司將逐步償還本金，Meta的租約承諾則支撐相關債務。相較無擔保公司借款，這些安排建立了更清楚的還款管道，但估值仍取決於資料中心的長期使用、租約持續性，以及有多少類似債券同時爭取相同買盤。

近期交易顯示，需求疲弱並非孤立現象。Amazon在7月稍早發行250億美元債券，訂單同樣僅為交易規模的1.6倍，遠低於2026年投資級債平均約4倍。Meta在4月的250億美元融資，定價利差比6個月前發行300億美元債券時更寬；Meta一檔2046年到期債券的利差，也較發行時擴大30個基點。市場仍能承接大規模發行，但隨AI資本需求累積，投資人要求的讓利也日益擴大。

這類供給正在改變高評級債券指數的風險構成。Barclays估計，截至7月23日，6大科技公司占美國高評級債券存續期間乘以利差曝險的8.6%，高於6大銀行的7.3%。超大規模雲端業者僅占市場本金約4%，低於大型銀行約9%，但其較長到期年限放大了影響力。過去12個月，超大規模雲端業者發行量有43%在10年後到期，高於併購債務的24%與其他非金融業供給的23%。

利差與發行趨勢讓集中度風險可以量化。科技投資級債利差7月23日約為89個基點，高於2026年初約76個基點。Barclays預估，今年超大規模雲端業者的全球投資級債發行額約2,850億美元。高評級借款人大量供給，即使未演變成違約週期，也足以損害報酬：較長存續期間與較寬新券利差可重新定價流通債券、推高指數層級的讓利，並壓縮其他發行人的融資容量。

個別借款人的困境則是另一條脈絡。Victoria因資產減記與減債相關成本，通報年度虧損3.263億英鎊。其再融資安排偏向部分債權人，並延長與2028年到期債券持有人的協商，直到HSBC提供支持後才得以推進重整。Charter Communications則在走到這一步以前，先處理到期日與法律實體的複雜性。公司提出交換或買回約$100億既有關係企業與Time Warner Cable債券，另有最高$97億其他子公司債務；最終將視參與情況發行最高$35億、2038年與2041年到期新債。交易可以延長並簡化債務結構，但不同順位與收購上限，意味各債權人的結果不一，也不是一致去槓桿。這些個案並非廣泛融資訊號，而是顯示即使初級市場仍對較強發行人開放，逼近的到期債務、法律實體與債權順位仍可能主導走勢。

中國銀行貸款定價改革，則以不同方式因應疲弱的信用需求。中國工商銀行、招商銀行與上海浦東發展銀行海口分行發放首批連結存款類機構回購利率的貸款，不再只依賴貸款市場報價利率。中國工商銀行的1年期貸款總額為人民幣7,670萬元，連結隔夜回購利率；上海浦東發展銀行貸款人民幣700萬元，招商銀行交易據報為人民幣800萬元。3月發放的貸款已有近50%定價低於LPR，高於2019年的16%。

貸款利率更直接連結市場交易的融資成本，可能改善貨幣政策傳導，尤其當銀行間利率與債券殖利率的降幅快於受管理的貸款基準。這也凸顯借款需求低迷已削弱LPR的參考價值。中美對比鮮明：中國貸款機構尋求更低、反應更即時的放款基準，美國科技借款人則支付更寬讓利，以取得超長期資金。

英國水務與德國工業信用顯示，新流動性可以與尚未解決的營運問題並存。已降至非投資等級的South East Water取得£2億未來發債backstop，用以支應現金與£19億投資計畫；但公司槓桿比率為66.5%，高於55%目標，先前服務中斷也使監管機構要求£3,050萬補償方案。BayWa在舉債進行全球擴張後，負債超過€100億；既有重整已要求銀行提供約€13億新債，下一階段則考慮把最高€7億貸款降為次順位，並要求股東投入至少€2.2億及出售資產。兩者都是以流動性延後懸崖，但營運修復與債權人損失分配仍未完成。Private credit買方結構也帶有自身誘因。Private equity對壽險公司的投資由2009年約$230億增至目前約$2,500億；以評級為基礎的保險資本規則，可能使客製化私人結構取得比風險相近公開債券更有利的資本計提。這類長期資金擴大融資容量，也使評級、保險公司所有權與監管待遇成為信用傳導的一部分。信用市場收盤時流動性運作正常，但「容易取得資金」的定義已經收窄。整體基金表現穩定，承壓的重整案件仍屬個別現象，具充分支持的專案依舊能募得大筆資金。日益關鍵的限制是新供給的規模、到期年限與集中度。高評級或租約承諾仍能打開市場，但當投資人必須反覆承接長存續期間AI融資時，兩者都無法阻止債券重新定價。

## 全球存續期間、央行與財政傳導

全球主權債賣壓依然強於週五美國公債漲勢。Bloomberg全球公債指數平均殖利率升至3.68%，創2008年以來最高；德國10年期殖利率升至2011年以來最高，英國基準殖利率維持在5%以上的時間為近20年來最久，日本超長天期公債價格也進一步走低。共同的能源壓力使各市場方向一致，但財政供給與國內政策可信度決定了變動幅度。

英國金邊債最明顯地同時承受通膨與財政風險。油價回落使10年期殖利率週五下降約4個基點，但全週維持在5%以上後，收盤仍接近5.04%。英國依賴能源進口，油價更容易傳導至家庭成本；首相Andy Burnham支出議程的不確定性，也引發市場對未來發債量的疑問。6月債務利息成本達118億英鎊，說明5%殖利率如何反向壓縮新計畫可用的財政空間。

資產負債表縮減進一步增加供給壓力。英國央行必須決定，從10月起的1年內要將剩餘4,920億英鎊金邊債投資組合縮減多少。本輪量化緊縮年度出售金額共210億英鎊，加上到期償還，整體部位減少700億英鎊；但明年贖回規模將大幅下降，同時債務管理辦公室規劃增加長天期發行。英國央行先前分析估計，量化緊縮已使10年期殖利率上升15至25個基點，因此縮減速度與年期配置將實質影響全球存續期間競爭。

歐元區的通膨訊號較為平衡。ECB在6月升息後維持利率不變，並保留9月調整的可能性，但6月消費者通膨預期在新一波油價衝擊前已經下降。1年期通膨預期由3.5%降至3%，3年期由2.9%降至2.8%。企業受訪者預期，薪資成長將由2025年的3.1%降至2026年的2.5%與2027年的2.4%，售價漲幅也低於預期。

這些調查未顯示已形成第2輪螺旋效應，因此削弱了央行立即緊縮的理由。不過，調查時點也限制了安定市場的效果：消費者調查於6月4日至29日進行，企業訪談則在7月1日結束，均早於最新一波油價急升。因此，ECB官員聚焦衝擊規模與持續時間，而非即期價格。衝擊前的通膨預期較低，讓央行有等待空間；但若能源價格再度持續上升，9月仍可能升息，而非按兵不動。政策操作框架也與利率討論同步調整。ECB開始讓外國央行加入強化版repo機制，預計自2026年第4季起由5個最大成員國央行執行，以支持政策傳導與歐元國際角色。ECB另把氣候因素擴及可作為抵押品的非金融企業信用債權，降低轉型衝擊造成抵押品價值下跌的風險。兩項措施都未改變週五政策利率，卻會調整壓力期間哪些抵押品與交易對手可取得歐元流動性。

日本同時面臨更直接的匯率傳導與財政疑慮。40年期JGB殖利率上升10個基點至4.01%，接近5月創下的4.355%紀錄；日圓貶至1美元兌163.99日圓，為1986年11月以來最低。能源進口成本上升、日圓走弱，都加大消費者物價壓力；減稅與國防支出的潛在資金來源尚未解決，則推高超長天期債務所需溢價。

日本央行6月將政策利率升至1%後，市場普遍預期7月31日會議將按兵不動，但利率市場仍定價年底前約32個基點的緊縮。半數受訪經濟學家仍預期12月才會再度升息，使市場定價與共識時程之間存在明顯落差。日本央行若加速緊縮，可能推高本地殖利率，降低避險後美國公債的相對吸引力；若延後緊縮，日圓可能進一步貶值，輸入型通膨則會透過另一條路徑延續相同的長端壓力。

各地經濟成長韌性並不一致，但仍避免全球債券走勢被完全解讀為停滯性通膨。馬來西亞第2季GDP年增5.8%，高於預期；內需、半導體投資與電子產品出口抵銷中東衝擊。歐元區民間部門活動升至5個月高點。即使油價與財政融資推高主權債投資人要求的殖利率，這些結果仍增強部分經濟體承受較高利率的能力。

Belgium與Russia顯示，財政或安全衝擊在真正發生再融資失敗前，就會壓縮政策選項。Morningstar DBRS維持Belgium的AA評級，但因公共債務達GDP的107.9%，且歐元區最高的5.2%赤字預計於2028年擴大至5.7%，把展望降至負向。執政聯盟計畫至2029年整頓€100億，但DBRS認為目前政治限制下，不太可能完成穩定債務所需的更大調整。Russia的季調年化通膨由前月2%升至6月10.6%，家庭通膨預期升至14.7%，攻擊干擾經濟後，汽油價格也比1年前高20%。央行決策前，選項已收窄至小幅降息或把利率維持在14.25%；財政部同時因投標疲弱暫停OFZ標售。高利率可保護匯率與預期，卻提高償債成本；在衝擊期間寬鬆則可能再次推高通膨與本地債殖利率。儘管週五油價帶來紓壓，全球市場對美國公債的淨傳導仍然不利。英國金邊債殖利率含有財政與量化緊縮溢價，JGB提供逐步上升的本地殖利率，ECB也保留再次升息的可能。這些市場都與美國公債爭奪全球資產負債表容量，使海外投資人配置美國存續期間的考量更為複雜。各國央行不必同步決策；只要不確定性與市場可取得的殖利率同步上升，就已足以壓抑需求。

## 新興市場主權債、美元流動性與債務管理風險

新興市場債券週五回穩，但週線背景仍具限制性。EMB單日上漲0.12%，此前1週下跌0.93%，1個月下跌1.68%。美元指數週五幾乎持平於101.47，但全週上漲0.71%。美元單日未大幅走強，有助硬通貨債券反彈；美國公債實質殖利率高檔與能源成本，則持續按照財政緩衝、進口曝險與市場融資能力區分各主權發行人。

馬來西亞證明，強健基本面仍可取得美元流動性。該國5年來首度發行美元債，透過伊斯蘭債券募得15億美元：其中8.5億美元債券於2032年4月到期，殖利率4.612%；另有6.5億美元券次於2036年7月到期，殖利率4.949%。訂單達發行額4.7倍，使最終定價較初始指引收窄30個基點。第2季5.8%的成長率支撐需求，但這筆融資也用於因應日益惡化的財政曝險。

能源衝擊可能使馬來西亞2026年汽油與柴油補貼成本升至400億令吉，超過150億令吉預算編列的2倍。因此，若油價維持高檔，這筆交易一方面反映穩健的市場融資能力，另一方面也伴隨財政結果惡化的可能。投資人願意按發行條件承接新增存續期間，是因經濟成長、政策可信度與伊斯蘭債券需求足以抵銷補貼風險；若油價衝擊延續至下一次預算，這項平衡將更難維持。

海灣發行人面對規模更大的同類債務管理問題。2026年區域債券發行已創下1,120億美元紀錄；沙烏地阿拉伯、科威特、阿拉伯聯合大公國與卡達均考慮新建可繞過荷姆茲海峽的港口、管線與道路。儘管遭受攻擊、石油出口嚴重受阻，科威特60億美元交易仍取得超過發行額2倍的投標；戰爭開始後不久，巴林也募得10億美元。即使面臨直接地緣政治壓力，信用評等與外匯存底仍維持其市場融資管道。

然而，供給已開始反映在利差中。阿布達比2054年到期債券相對美國公債利差約82個基點，高於1月的53個基點，既反映衝突風險，也反映增發預期。地理條件同樣重要，因為沙烏地阿拉伯、阿拉伯聯合大公國與阿曼取得替代路線的條件優於科威特、巴林與卡達。紅海攻擊顯示，繞道基礎設施只能重新分配風險，無法消除風險；因此，以舉債支應的韌性建設既能支撐信用，也會形成未來供給。

新興市場呈現分化，而非共同的融資斷裂。週五美元持穩、主權債訂單強勁，顯示高評級發行人仍能進入市場。但美國實質殖利率高檔、補貼支出增加，以及海灣地區發行量創紀錄，仍推高成交成本，使資產負債表較強的發行人更受青睞。最脆弱的情境，是能源衝擊同時削弱財政帳戶，以及賺取外匯所仰賴的實體運輸路線。

## 跨資產

跨資產表現證實，週五是油價回落帶來的紓壓交易，並非市場全面恢復風險偏好。布蘭特原油下跌3.88%，WTI下跌3.12%，帶動美國公債上漲、10年期損益兩平通膨率收斂。S&P 500幾乎持平，VIX則下降0.64%至18.58。這些走勢不符合被迫平倉或普遍性融資衝擊的特徵。

科技股呈現主要矛盾。Nasdaq 100下跌1.15%，費城半導體指數下跌4.25%，1個月跌幅擴大至12.34%；同一時間，涵蓋範圍更廣的S&P 500卻持平。這項分歧把市場對AI投資回報的疑慮，連結到信用市場難以反覆承接長天期科技債融資的問題。股市壓力集中在資本支出與債券供給最大的領域，而不是理應最直接受惠於能源價格回落的領域。

美元與黃金顯示，政策不確定性仍在發揮作用。美元指數週五僅變動0.04%，但全週上漲0.71%；黃金在稍早走弱後，上漲0.52%至4,067.60美元。美元持穩，限制新興市場債券的單日壓力；油價下跌之際黃金上漲，則反映地緣政治避險需求延續。整體訊息是選擇性重新定價：能源通膨的邊際壓力下降，但AI集中度、Fed不確定性與長存續期間供給仍未解決。

## 前瞻市場意義

7月28日至29日FOMC決策，加上未來一週公布的第2季GDP與6月通膨數據，將決定週五牛市趨陡是否不只是油價回吐。市場預估第2季年化成長率接近2.1%，並預期6月通膨放緩；但利率能否突破當前門檻，取決於數據公布後油價與關稅定價的交互作用。若Fed按兵不動並強調基礎通膨受控，同時布蘭特原油維持在100美元以下、2年期與10年期實質殖利率下降，本週累積的政策溢價將進一步回吐。若Fed升息、鷹派按兵不動，或經濟活動強韌又遇能源壓力升高，2年期仍將位於調整核心，2s10s也可能再次趨平。決定性的變化必須來自實質殖利率，因為週五紓壓只靠損益兩平通膨率收斂。

預計7月27日定價的123億美元Sopaipilla資料中心融資，以及隨後Microsoft、Meta與Amazon更新支出展望，將直接檢驗AI借款究竟只形成發行人層級的讓利，還是已成為整體指數的限制。若交易接近指引的287.5個基點利差完成定價，且次級市場表現穩定，代表租約支持與攤還安排足以克服僅1.6倍的訂單。若成交利差更寬、發行規模縮減或交易延後，或長天期超大規模雲端業者債券再度走弱，股市對AI報酬的疑慮便會連結到更高融資成本，並壓縮其他投資級發行人的融資容量。科技債利差、長存續期間公司債，以及後續新券讓利將傳遞關鍵訊號。

英國央行7月30日決策與日本央行7月31日決策，將檢驗美國公債期限溢價論點中的全球因素。若英國央行指引把油價回落視為暫時現象，或日本央行面對接近1美元兌164日圓的匯率採取更鷹派立場，其他主權債殖利率將上升，進一步壓抑海外對美國公債的需求。若市場更相信英國成長將受到抑制、英國央行放慢資產負債表縮減，或日本央行訊息維持以12月為中心的升息路徑，金邊債與超長天期JGB若上漲，便可降低這項競爭。匯率反應不可或缺：日圓走強顯示政策可信度正降低輸入型通膨；若持續貶值，日本的利率與海外資產配置管道仍未化解。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The July 24 Treasury close delivered a modest bull-steepening after 3 consecutive sessions of front-led losses, but it did not reverse the week’s policy repricing. The 2-year yield fell 4 basis points to 4.33%, the 10-year declined 2 basis points to 4.69%, and the 30-year eased 1 basis point to 5.16%. Brent’s retreat to $96.78 removed some immediate inflation pressure after its break above $100, allowing the policy-sensitive sector to recover most. Yet yields still ended 10 to 15 basis points higher over the week, the 10-year real yield remained at 2.43%, and the long bond stayed near levels last seen almost 2 decades ago.

The composition of Friday’s rally defines the central interpretation. The 10-year nominal yield fell entirely through a 2-basis-point decline in breakeven inflation to 2.26%; the real yield was unchanged. Oil’s 3.88% daily fall reduced the marginal inflation impulse, but Brent remained 9.85% higher over 1 week and 25.56% higher over 1 month. Markets still assigned roughly a 35% probability to a July Fed increase, compared with about 10% after the cooler June CPI release. The prior close’s rise in real yields was therefore paused, not unwound, and the bar for a durable duration rally remained high.

The inflation distribution also broadened beyond energy. Duties of 10% to 12.5% on imports from about 60 economies took effect as Washington rebuilt part of its tariff regime. Those levies introduced a prospective goods-price channel just as resilient US services activity and higher new-home sales limited the growth case for rapid easing. Neither the tariffs nor oil had established a renewed acceleration in underlying inflation by the close. Their coexistence, combined with reduced Fed forward guidance, made the July 28-29 decision unusually difficult to anchor and kept expected Treasury volatility elevated.

Credit resisted a systemic tightening interpretation, but the calm in broad gauges concealed a more important change in absorption. Investment-grade and high-yield funds were almost flat on Friday, while a $12.3 billion bond financing for a Meta data-center project attracted orders of only 1.6 times the amount offered. Long-dated technology supply is becoming an index-level duration issue: the 6 largest technology borrowers now account for 8.6% of US high-grade duration-times-spread risk, more than the 7.3% share of the 6 largest banks. Capital remained available, but concession, lease support and concentration were replacing credit quality alone as the binding questions.

Global duration supplied a further limit on the Treasury rally. UK 10-year yields stayed above 5% despite easing on Friday, Japan’s 40-year yield rose 10 basis points to 4.01%, and the average yield on an investment-grade global sovereign benchmark reached 3.68%, the highest since 2008. The ECB’s pre-oil surveys showed softer inflation expectations and wage growth, but officials kept September tightening open. The close was consequently a controlled relief move inside a global inflation, fiscal and capital-supply regime that still demanded unusually high real yields.

## UST Rates, Fed Pricing, Real Yields, And Curve Structure

Treasuries reversed part of Thursday’s selloff in an orderly maturity sequence. The 2-year yield declined 4 basis points to 4.33%, the 5-year fell 3 basis points to 4.43%, the 10-year eased 2 basis points to 4.69%, and the 30-year slipped 1 basis point to 5.16%. The 2s10s curve steepened 2 basis points to 36, while 2s30s steepened 3 basis points to 83. Front-end outperformance was the mirror image of the prior session’s bear flattening: the immediate policy premium softened as crude retreated, while long-end compensation proved more persistent.

That daily relief was small relative to the accumulated move. Over 1 week, the 2- and 5-year yields each rose 15 basis points, the 10-year increased 14, and the 30-year added 10. Over 1 month, the rises were 17, 16, 19 and 22 basis points. The weekly pattern still reflected a forceful adjustment toward a firmer policy path; the monthly pattern preserved a larger rise at the long end, where fiscal borrowing, global sovereign supply and corporate capital expenditure compete for duration capacity.

Inflation-linked Treasuries showed that Friday’s rally was a retracement of the energy premium rather than a reduction in the real-rate hurdle. The 10-year real yield held at 2.43%, 12 basis points above its level 1 week earlier and 14 basis points higher over 1 month. The 10-year breakeven fell 2 basis points to 2.26%, leaving it only 2 basis points higher over the week. A contained medium-term inflation gauge alongside a very high real yield indicates that investors had not abandoned confidence in long-run price control; they were charging heavily for the policy and growth uncertainty required to achieve it.

The oil path explains the distinction between Friday and the week. Brent closed at $96.78 and WTI at $89.31, down 3.88% and 3.12% on the day as physical flows continued through Middle East routes and discussion of renewed mediation offered some relief. Earlier attacks had extended the conflict from Hormuz toward Red Sea shipping and driven Brent above $100. The daily decline reduced the urgency of the inflation tail, but the weekly gains of 9.85% in Brent and 8.27% in WTI left fuel, freight and inventory costs materially above the prior Friday.

Fed pricing therefore remained asymmetric even as yields declined. Roughly 35% odds of a 25-basis-point increase at the July meeting reflected the combination of elevated oil, new tariffs and uncertainty created by Chairman Kevin Warsh’s reduced use of forward guidance. The probability was not a consensus expectation of a hike. It represented a much wider outcome distribution than after June CPI, when market odds had fallen to roughly 10%, and it helped lift the MOVE Index to its highest level since May.

Domestic activity limited the scope of Friday’s rally. US business activity expanded at its fastest pace in 8 months as services demand offset cooler manufacturing, and new-home sales increased. Those signals did not establish overheating, but they made it harder to assume that an external supply shock was landing on collapsing demand. A resilient activity base gives the Fed more room to prioritize prospective inflation, which helps explain why the 2-year could rally on lower oil without returning to levels seen before the week’s escalation.

Tariffs added a slower and less certain transmission channel. Duties of 10% to 12.5% replaced an expiring 10% global import tax and covered goods from about 60 economies. The measures were operative by Friday, but their effect on consumer prices, margins and trade volumes remained prospective. For rates, the immediate consequence was not a realized inflation print; it was a broader range around the policy path because energy and import costs could reinforce each other even if either shock alone proved temporary.

The long end remained the principal valuation constraint. At 5.16%, the 30-year yield fell only 1 basis point on a day when oil retreated sharply, and the 20-year-plus Treasury index was still down 1.48% over 1 week and 4.39% over 1 month. That persistence fits a market in which global governments and technology issuers are asking overlapping pools of insurers, pensions and long-duration funds to absorb more supply. Friday’s curve steepening was therefore relief at the front end, not a restoration of an easy long-bond demand function.

The Treasury close reconciles the apparent tension between lower daily yields and a more restrictive weekly regime. Breakeven compression allowed a partial rally, while unchanged 10-year real yields, elevated Fed uncertainty and a stubborn 30-year level prevented the move from becoming a broad reassessment of policy or term premium. A lasting reversal requires either a sustained retreat in the energy and tariff inflation channels or a clear deterioration in activity sufficient to pull real yields lower.

## Credit, Funding, And Primary-Market Absorption

Broad credit finished Friday without a disorderly risk premium. LQD slipped 0.03%, HYG was unchanged, and JNK fell 0.01%. Over 1 month, the larger 2.46% decline in LQD versus losses of 0.80% in HYG and 0.89% in JNK primarily reflected the heavier duration burden carried by investment grade. Credit spreads were still near their tightest levels in years at the broad-market level. The more consequential signal came from the terms needed to distribute long-dated AI infrastructure debt.

BlackRock’s planned financing for a Meta data-center campus in El Paso drew $20 billion of final orders against $12.3 billion of bonds, only 1.6 times the offered amount. The notes, issued through Sopaipilla Investor and due in 2048, were guided around 287.5 basis points over 10-year Treasuries. That concession was about 40 basis points wider than a comparable Beignet note due in 2049, whose spread had already widened by more than 50 basis points during July. Pricing was expected on July 27 rather than completed by Friday’s close.

The structure supplied genuine creditor protection without eliminating the concentration problem. Proceeds finance a campus expected to provide as much as 1 gigawatt of computing capacity. BlackRock subsidiaries hold 80% of the project and Meta owns 20%. The special-purpose vehicle gradually repays principal, and Meta’s lease commitments support the obligations. Those features create a clearer payment channel than unsecured corporate borrowing, but they still leave valuation tied to long-term data-center use, lease durability and the amount of similar paper competing for the same buyers.

Recent transactions show that weak demand was not isolated. Amazon’s $25 billion offering earlier in July also drew orders equal to only 1.6 times the deal, compared with a 2026 investment-grade average of roughly 4 times. Meta’s $25 billion April financing priced at wider spreads than its $30 billion sale 6 months earlier, and a Meta note due in 2046 had widened by 30 basis points from issuance. The market remained open at scale; it was requiring larger concessions as AI capital needs accumulated.

That supply is changing the composition of high-grade index risk. Barclays estimated that the 6 largest technology companies represented 8.6% of US high-grade duration-times-spread exposure as of July 23, exceeding the 7.3% contribution from the 6 largest banks. Hyperscalers account for only about 4% of market principal, compared with roughly 9% for the largest banks, but their longer maturities amplify their influence. During the past 12 months, 43% of hyperscaler issuance matured beyond 10 years, versus 24% for M&A debt and 23% for other nonfinancial supply.

The spread and issuance trajectories make the concentration measurable. Technology investment-grade spreads reached about 89 basis points on July 23, up from around 76 at the start of 2026. Barclays projected roughly $285 billion of global investment-grade issuance from hyperscalers this year. Heavy supply from highly rated borrowers need not become a default cycle to damage returns: longer duration and wider new-issue levels can reprice outstanding bonds, raise index concessions and reduce capacity available to unrelated issuers.

Borrower-specific distress remained a separate lane. Victoria reported a £326.3 million annual loss after writedowns and costs associated with reducing debt. Its refinancing favored some creditors over others, extending negotiations with holders of 2028 notes until HSBC’s support allowed the restructuring to proceed. Charter Communications addressed maturity and entity complexity before reaching that stage. It offered to exchange or repurchase about $10 billion of existing affiliate and Time Warner Cable bonds plus as much as $9.7 billion of other subsidiary debt, with up to $3.5 billion of new 2038 and 2041 notes depending on participation. The transaction could extend and simplify the stack, but different priority levels and caps meant outcomes would vary across holders rather than produce uniform deleveraging. These cases were not broad funding signals. They showed how looming maturities, legal entity and creditor ranking can dominate even when primary markets remain available to stronger issuers.

China’s bank-loan pricing reform pointed to a different response to weak credit demand. ICBC, China Merchants Bank and Shanghai Pudong Development Bank’s Haikou branch issued initial loans linked to depository-institution repo rates instead of relying solely on the loan prime rate. ICBC’s 1-year facility totaled 76.7 million yuan and was tied to the overnight repo rate; SPDB lent 7 million yuan, and the China Merchants transaction was reported at 8 million yuan. Nearly 50% of loans issued in March had already priced below the LPR, up from 16% in 2019.

Linking loans more directly to traded funding costs may improve transmission where interbank rates and bond yields have fallen faster than the administered lending benchmark. It also exposes how subdued borrower demand has weakened the LPR’s relevance. The contrast with the US is sharp: Chinese lenders were seeking a lower, more responsive lending reference, while US technology borrowers were paying wider concessions to secure very long capital.

UK water and German industrial credit showed how new liquidity could coexist with an unresolved operating problem. Junk-rated South East Water secured a £200 million backstop for a future bond sale to support cash and a £1.9 billion investment plan, but gearing was 66.5% versus a 55% target and regulators had imposed a £30.5 million redress package after service failures. BayWa's liabilities exceeded €10 billion after debt-funded global expansion; a restructuring had already required about €1.3 billion of fresh bank debt, and the next plan contemplated subordinating as much as €700 million of loans plus at least €220 million of shareholder capital and asset sales. In each case, liquidity delayed the cliff while operating repair and creditor loss allocation remained unfinished. The private-credit buyer base carried its own structural incentive. Private-equity investment in life insurers had increased from about $23 billion in 2009 to roughly $250 billion, and rating-based insurance capital rules can reward bespoke private structures with more favorable charges than comparably risky public bonds. That permanent capital expands funding capacity but makes ratings, insurer ownership and regulatory treatment part of the underlying credit transmission. Credit ended the session with functioning liquidity but a narrower definition of easy access. Broad funds were stable, stressed restructurings remained idiosyncratic, and well-supported projects could still raise large sums. The binding constraint was increasingly the amount, maturity and concentration of new supply. A high rating or lease commitment still opened the market, but neither prevented repricing when investors had to absorb repeated long-duration AI transactions.

## Global Duration, Central Banks, And Fiscal Transmission

The global sovereign selloff remained more powerful than Friday’s US rally. The average yield on the Bloomberg Global Treasury Index reached 3.68%, its highest since 2008, as German 10-year yields traded at their highest since 2011, UK benchmark yields spent their longest stretch above 5% in almost 2 decades, and Japan’s super-long curve cheapened. Common energy pressure synchronized the direction of travel, but fiscal supply and domestic policy credibility determined the magnitude.

UK gilts carried the clearest mix of inflation and fiscal risk. The 10-year yield fell about 4 basis points on Friday as oil eased, yet it remained near 5.04% after holding above 5% throughout the week. Britain’s energy-import dependence increases the pass-through from oil into household costs, while uncertainty over Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s spending agenda raised questions about future issuance. June debt-service costs of £11.8 billion illustrated how a 5% yield feeds back into the fiscal room available for new programs.

Balance-sheet runoff adds to that supply pressure. The Bank of England must decide how much of its remaining £492 billion gilt portfolio to reduce in the year beginning in October. Sales totaled £21 billion in the current quantitative-tightening year, and maturities allowed an overall £70 billion reduction, but redemptions fall sharply next year as the Debt Management Office plans more long-dated issuance. Prior BOE analysis estimated that quantitative tightening had added 15 to 25 basis points to 10-year yields, making the pace and maturity mix consequential for global duration competition.

The euro area presented a more balanced inflation signal. The ECB held rates after its June increase and kept a possible September move open, but June consumer expectations moved lower before the renewed oil shock. The 1-year expectation fell to 3% from 3.5%, and the 3-year measure eased to 2.8% from 2.9%. Corporate respondents expected wage growth of 2.5% in 2026 and 2.4% in 2027 after 3.1% in 2025, while selling-price growth was less pronounced than anticipated.

Those surveys constrain the case for automatic tightening because they show no established 2nd-round spiral. Their timing also limits reassurance: the consumer poll ran from June 4 to June 29, and the corporate conversations ended July 1, before the latest surge in oil. ECB officials consequently focused on the size and duration of the shock rather than its spot price. Lower pre-shock expectations provide room to wait, but another sustained energy rise could still make September a hike rather than a hold. The operating framework was evolving alongside the rate debate. The ECB began onboarding foreign central banks for an enhanced repo facility available from Q4 2026 through the 5 largest national central banks, intended to support policy transmission and the euro's international role. It also extended climate factors to nonfinancial corporate credit claims used as collateral, protecting central banks against transition-related valuation losses. Neither step changed Friday's policy rate, but both altered which collateral and counterparties could obtain euro liquidity under stress.

Japan combined a more immediate currency channel with fiscal concern. The 40-year JGB yield rose 10 basis points to 4.01%, near the 4.355% record reached in May, as the yen weakened to 163.99 per dollar, its lowest level since November 1986. Higher energy import costs and a weaker currency increase pressure on consumer prices, while unresolved funding for prospective tax cuts and defense spending raises the premium attached to super-long debt.

Markets priced about 32 basis points of BOJ tightening by year-end even though the central bank was widely expected to hold on July 31 after raising its policy rate to 1% in June. Half of surveyed economists still expected the next increase in December, leaving a meaningful gap between market pricing and the consensus calendar. A faster BOJ path could raise local yields and reduce the relative attraction of hedged Treasuries; delayed tightening could allow further yen depreciation and imported inflation to sustain the same long-end pressure through a different route.

Growth resilience was not uniform but prevented the global bond move from being read solely as stagflation. Malaysia’s GDP rose 5.8% from a year earlier in Q2, beating expectations as domestic demand, semiconductor investment and electronics exports offset the Middle East shock. In the euro area, private-sector activity reached a 5-month high. These outcomes strengthened the capacity of some economies to absorb higher rates even as oil and fiscal borrowing raised the yield required by sovereign investors.

Belgium and Russia showed how fiscal or security shocks can narrow policy choices before a refinancing failure occurs. Morningstar DBRS kept Belgium at AA but moved the outlook to negative as public debt reached 107.9% of GDP and a 5.2% deficit—the euro area's largest—was projected to widen to 5.7% by 2028. The coalition sought €10 billion of consolidation through 2029, yet DBRS judged a larger adjustment unlikely under current political constraints. In Russia, seasonally adjusted annualized inflation accelerated to 10.6% in June, household expectations rose to 14.7% and gasoline was 20% more expensive than a year earlier after attacks disrupted the economy. Ahead of the central-bank decision, the choice had narrowed to a small cut or a pause at 14.25%, while the Finance Ministry had already halted OFZ auctions amid weak bids. Higher rates protect the currency and expectations but worsen debt service; easing into the shock risks another inflation and local-bond repricing. The net transmission to Treasuries remained adverse despite Friday’s oil relief. Gilts offered a fiscal and quantitative-tightening premium, JGBs offered progressively higher domestic yields, and the ECB preserved another possible increase. These markets compete with Treasuries for global balance-sheet capacity and complicate foreign demand for US duration. A synchronized policy decision was unnecessary; a synchronized increase in uncertainty and available yield was sufficient.

## EM Sovereigns, Dollar Liquidity, And Debt-Management Risk

Emerging-market debt stabilized on Friday, but the weekly backdrop remained restrictive. EMB rose 0.12% on the day after falling 0.93% over 1 week and 1.68% over 1 month. The Dollar Index was almost unchanged at 101.47 on Friday but gained 0.71% over the week. The absence of a daily dollar surge helped hard-currency debt recover, while high Treasury real yields and energy costs continued to separate sovereigns by fiscal buffers, import exposure and market access.

Malaysia demonstrated that strong fundamentals could still secure dollar liquidity. Its 1st dollar sale in 5 years raised $1.5 billion through sukuk: an $850 million note due in April 2032 yielded 4.612%, and a $650 million tranche due in July 2036 yielded 4.949%. Orders reached 4.7 times the sale, allowing final pricing to tighten 30 basis points from initial indications. The 5.8% Q2 growth rate supported demand, but the financing also addressed a worsening fiscal exposure.

The energy shock could lift Malaysia’s petrol and diesel subsidy cost to 40 billion ringgit in 2026, more than 2 times the 15 billion ringgit budget allocation. Its transaction therefore joined strong market access with a potentially weaker fiscal outcome if oil remains elevated. Investors accepted the new duration because growth, policy credibility and sukuk demand outweighed the subsidy risk at the offered terms; that balance becomes less comfortable if the oil shock persists into the next budget.

Gulf issuers faced a larger version of the same debt-management problem. Regional bond sales had already reached a record $112 billion in 2026 as Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the UAE and Qatar considered new ports, pipelines and roads that bypass Hormuz. Kuwait’s $6 billion transaction drew bids exceeding 2 times the amount offered despite attacks and severely disrupted oil exports, while Bahrain raised $1 billion soon after the war began. Ratings and foreign-exchange reserves preserved access even under direct geopolitical pressure.

Supply was nevertheless entering spreads. Abu Dhabi’s 2054 bonds traded about 82 basis points over Treasuries, compared with 53 basis points in January, reflecting both conflict risk and expectations of more issuance. Geography also mattered because Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Oman have better access to alternative routes than Kuwait, Bahrain and Qatar. The Red Sea attacks showed that bypass infrastructure can redistribute exposure without eliminating it, making debt-funded resilience projects both a credit support and a source of future supply.

The EM conclusion was dispersion rather than a common funding break. A stable dollar on Friday and strong sovereign orderbooks showed that high-grade issuers retained access. Elevated US real yields, larger subsidy bills and record Gulf supply still raised the clearing cost and rewarded stronger balance sheets. The main vulnerability lay where an energy shock weakened both the fiscal account and the physical route needed to earn foreign currency.

## Cross asset

Cross assets confirmed that Friday was an oil-relief session without a broad return to risk. Brent fell 3.88% and WTI declined 3.12%, helping Treasuries rally and 10-year breakevens compress. The S&P 500 was nearly unchanged, and the VIX fell 0.64% to 18.58. Those moves were inconsistent with forced liquidation or a generalized funding shock.

Technology delivered the principal contradiction. The Nasdaq 100 fell 1.15%, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 4.25%, extending its 1-month decline to 12.34%, even as the broader S&P 500 held flat. The split connected concern about AI returns to the credit market’s difficulty absorbing repeated long-dated technology financings. Equity stress was concentrated where capital expenditure and debt supply were largest, not where the energy retreat should have delivered the most immediate relief.

The dollar and gold showed that policy uncertainty remained active. The Dollar Index changed only 0.04% on Friday but ended 0.71% higher over 1 week, while gold rose 0.52% to $4,067.60 after earlier weakness. A stable dollar limited the daily pressure on EM debt, and higher gold alongside lower oil reflected continued geopolitical hedging. The combined message was a selective repricing: energy inflation eased at the margin, but AI concentration, Fed uncertainty and long-duration supply remained unresolved.

## Forward Market Significance

The July 28-29 FOMC decision, accompanied in the coming week by Q2 GDP and June inflation data, determines whether Friday’s bull-steepening becomes more than an oil retracement. Market forecasts placed annualized Q2 growth near 2.1% and anticipated slower June inflation, but the rates threshold is the interaction with post-release oil and tariff pricing. A hold that emphasizes contained underlying inflation, alongside Brent remaining below $100 and a decline in 2-year and 10-year real yields, would unwind more of the week’s policy premium. A hike, a hawkish hold, or resilient activity combined with renewed energy pressure would keep the 2-year near the center of the adjustment and could flatten 2s10s again. The decisive change would be movement in real yields, because breakeven compression alone produced Friday’s relief.

The $12.3 billion Sopaipilla data-center financing expected to price on July 27, followed by spending updates from Microsoft, Meta and Amazon, provides a direct test of whether AI borrowing remains an issuer-level concession or becomes an index-wide constraint. Pricing near the indicated 287.5-basis-point spread with stable secondary performance would show that lease support and amortization can overcome a 1.6-times orderbook. A wider clearing level, size delay or renewed weakness in long-dated hyperscaler bonds would connect equity doubts about AI returns to higher funding costs and reduced capacity for other investment-grade issuers. Technology spreads, the long-duration corporate complex and subsequent new-issue concessions carry the signal.

The Bank of England decision on July 30 and the Bank of Japan decision on July 31 test the global part of the Treasury term-premium story. BOE guidance that treats the oil retreat as temporary, or a more hawkish BOJ stance against a yen near 164 per dollar, would raise competing sovereign yields and reinforce the pressure on foreign demand for Treasuries. Greater confidence in UK growth restraint, slower BOE balance-sheet reduction, or a BOJ message that preserves a December-centered path would reduce that competition if gilts and super-long JGBs rally. Currency response is integral: a firmer yen would show that policy credibility is easing imported inflation, while continued depreciation would leave Japan’s rate and foreign-allocation channels unresolved.

overall_summary.session_narrative: At the July 24 NY close, Treasuries bull-steepened as the retreat in oil eased the immediate inflation tail and allowed the policy-sensitive front end to recover. The rally came through lower breakevens rather than lower 10-year real yields, so resilient activity, operative tariffs and uncertain Fed guidance continued to support a wide policy distribution. Stable credit gauges ruled out broad funding stress, yet heavy technology borrowing and competing global sovereign yields limited long-duration demand.
overall_summary.summary: Treasuries recovered after 3 sessions of front-led losses as lower oil compressed inflation compensation, yet unchanged real yields left the week's policy repricing intact. Stable broad credit limited systemic concern, although long-duration technology supply and firmer global sovereign yields kept absorption and term premium restrictive.
